items.name: Dispersion (optics)

clues.text: This phenomenon is minimized at a characteristic value of 1300 nanometers in a silica optical fiber, whose "modal" type occurs due to polarizations in a waveguide.

clues.label: Abbe
clues.text: Measurements of three Fraunhofer lines are used to calculate a measure of this phenomenon called the Abbe ("ABB-uh") number.

clues.text: The functions relating angular frequency and wavenumber are called this phenomenon's "relations."

clues.label: anomalous
clues.text: The rapid variation of the dielectric function over a narrow frequency range is known as the "anomalous" variant of this phenomenon.

clues.label: Cauchy's
clues.text: An equation modelling this phenomenon contains a term summing Bλ2("B-lambda-squared")over the quantity λ2("lambda-squared") minus C and built off of Cauchy's ("koh-SHEEZ") equation.

related.name: Optical fiber
related.why: Optical fibers are designed so the "material" and "waveguide" forms of this phenomenon cancel out.

related.name: Refractive index
related.why: This phenomenon occurs when light's refractive index varies with wavelength.

related.name: Group velocity
related.why: Group velocity can be calculated by differentiating a "relation" named for this phenomenon.

related.name: Angular frequency
related.why: Any relation between angular frequency and wavenumber is named for this phenomenon.

related.name: Snell's law
related.why: This phenomenon occurs when a medium's index of refraction is dependent on the wavelength, thus causing a non-coherent light beam to separate since Snell's law implies the different wavelengths refract at different angles.

items.name: Lombards

clues.text: Kings of these people include Alboin, Liutprand, and a man who was defeated by Charlemagne, Desiderius.

clues.label: Rosamund
clues.text: A king of these people was killed after inviting his wife Rosamund to drink from the skull of her father.

clues.text: The depopulation caused by the long Gothic Wars allowed this people to swiftly defeat the Byzantines and established a kingdom under Alboin ruled from the city of Pavia.

clues.label: Rothari
clues.text: These people had officials called gastalds, which were granted authority by the Edict of Rothari.

related.name: Pepin the Short

related.name: Sigmund Freud

items.name: Microscopy
items.description: technical field of using microscopes to view samples and objects that cannot be seen with the unaided eye

clues.label: transmission
clues.text: Samples are sputter-coated with gold in types of this technique named for "scanning" and "transmission."

clues.label: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek
clues.text: This technique was popularized by Antonie van Leeuwenhoek and Robert Hooke, who used it to discover the cell.

clues.label: atomic force
clues.text: The subtle movement of a sharp cantilever is central to the "atomic force" type of this technique.

clues.label: cryogenic
clues.text: The sample is vitrified [VIH-trih-fyde] using liquid ethane in a form of this technique termed "cryogenic."

clues.text: A type of this technique has an "acoustic" variant in which the sample is placed on a piezoelectric transducer.

related.name: Robert Hooke

clues.text: This character is killed for trying to describe a "terrible fowl"-also known as a hot air balloon-in a story by Edgar Allen Poe.

clues.label: John Barth's Chimera

clues.label: Tell whoso hath sorrow / Grief never shall last

clues.label: Open sesame

related.name: One Thousand and One Nights

items.name: Rutherford scattering experiments
items.description: series of experiments (1908–1913) by Hans Geiger and Ernest Marsden, directed by Ernest Rutherford, at the University of Manchester, proving the existence of the atomic nucleus through alpha particle scattering on gold foil

clues.label: Geiger and Marsden
clues.text: A tube containing radium and bismuth-214 was a component of this experiment's setup, which is sometimes also named after Geiger and Marsden.

clues.label: reciprocal of the fourth power of the sine of the half angle
clues.text: The differential cross section of this process is proportional to the "reciprocal of the fourth power of the sine of the half angle."

clues.label: Nondestructive thin film analysis using this process usually…
clues.text: Nondestructive thin film analysis using this process usually uses an energy of two to three megaelectronvolts, can be improved by ion channeling, and plots count against either channels or energy.

clues.label: Mott
clues.text: Mott scattering is the equivalent of this process in electrons.

clues.label: Schrodinger's
clues.text: A device central to the setup of Schrodinger's cat was developed as a result of this experiment.

related.name: Ernest Rutherford
related.why: For 10 points, name this procedure in which alpha particles were fired at the namesake metal, an experiment credited to Ernest Rutherford.

related.name: Atomic nucleus
related.why: This experiment led to the discovery of the atomic nucleus.

related.name: Alpha particle
related.why: In this experiment, the namesake apparatus was bombarded with alpha particles, some of which bounced off at surprising angles.

related.name: Hans Geiger
related.why: This experiment was performed by Hans Geiger and Ernest Marsden, and it helped disprove the plum pudding model of the atom.

related.name: Charles-Augustin de Coulomb
related.why: For 10 points, name this scattering of charged particles by the Coulomb potential of the nucleus, which was used to infer the existence of the nucleus.

items.name: Transverse flute

clues.text: Over 300 concertos for this instrument were written by Johann Joachim Quantz ("k'VONTS"), who taught Frederick the Great to play it.

clues.label: Georges Barrere
clues.text: Georges Barrere commissioned Edgar Varese's Density 21.5 for this instrument, and also premiered a chromatic line descending from C-sharp to G in one symphonic poem.

clues.label: Afternoon
clues.text: The melody begins on this instrument in Bolero, and it also opens Debussy's Prelude to the Afternoon of a Faun.

clues.label: Largo
clues.text: This instrument follows the violin two bars later and a fourth higher in a canon that opens the "Largo" first movement of a trio sonata embedded within The Musical Offering.

clues.label: Domenico Cimarosa
clues.text: Two of these instruments are the soloists in the only fully authenticated concerto by Domenico Cimarosa ("chee-mah-ROH-zah").

related.name: Prélude à l'après-midi d'un faune
related.why: that piece, also by Debussy, is Prelude to the Afternoon of a Faun.

related.name: Boléro
related.why: The melody begins on this instrument in Bolero, and it also opens Debussy's Prelude to the Afternoon of a Faun.

related.name: The Musical Offering
related.why: This instrument follows the violin two bars later and a fourth higher in a canon that opens the "Largo" first movement of a trio sonata embedded within The Musical Offering.

related.name: Jean-Pierre Rampal
related.why: This instrument often features a "gizmo key" that makes playing a high C easier, and one of these made of solid gold was owned by Jean-Pierre Rampal.

related.name: Cécile Chaminade
related.why: A concertino for this instrument opens with an orchestral descending D major scale and was composed by Cecile Chaminade.

items.name: Sorting algorithm
items.description: algorithm that puts elements of a list in a certain order

clues.label: Big O
clues.text: Big O of n-squared describes the worst-case runtime of the "quick" form of this algorithm.

clues.label: quick
clues.text: One task of this type uses a pivot and is called the "quick" type.

clues.label: rises
clues.text: One type of this algorithm is named because it "rises" elements to the top,and is called bubble.

clues.label: Donald Shell
clues.text: Another way to perform this operation relies on gap sequences and was formulated by Donald Shell.

clues.label: radix
clues.text: A variation of this operation that can compare least significant digits is called the radix type, and another type of this process randomly places elements and checks if they are correct.

related.name: Time complexity
related.why: Algorithms for this task that use comparisons have a best-case runtime of big-omega of n log n, although this is avoided by the counting kind of this type of algorithm.

related.name: John von Neumann
related.why: An algorithm for this task developed by John von Neumann recursively divides a list into halves and then merges the lists together.

related.name: Heap (data structure)
related.why: These structures are used in a sorting algorithm which removes the maximal element from one of these structures, puts it at the end of the sorted list, and rebuilds one of these structures;

related.name: Quicksort
related.why: For 10 points, name this algorithm, the fastest sorting algorithm known.

related.name: Python (programming language)
related.why: Python's standard algorithm for this task, which was developed by, and named for, Tim Peters, preserves 'runs' and is thus considered 'stable'.

clues.label: nodules
clues.text: Fungi form symbiotic relationships with these structures in mycorrhizae, and rhizobia, which fix nitrogen, form nodules on them.

clues.label: cap
clues.text: The "cap" of these organs contains columella cells which sense gravity using auxins.

clues.label: tap
clues.text: Monocots typically have a "fibrous" system of these structures, while the "tap" form of these structures is exemplified by carrots.

clues.label: Hartig
clues.text: These structures are penetrated by Hartig nets and secrete mucigel.

clues.label: aerial
clues.text: Epiphytes often have "aerial" examples of these organs, and certain mangroves have upward-growing examples called pneumatophores [noo-MAT-uh-forz].

related.name: Meristem
related.why: These structures contain a quiescent center of low mitotic activity surrounded by an apical meristem that produces cells in two directions.
